reviews.text: Jenkins doesn’t rely on pity to make Moonlight dramatically engaging. Instead, he pours out an aura of compassion that naturally renders this film poignant. On top of that, the cinematography and lighting is exhilarating in this film.
reviews.author: JD Duran

reviews.text: Moonlight is filmmaking poetry, and a perfect movie.
reviews.author: Brendan Cassidy

reviews.text: A profoundly moving coming-of-age portrait of a young Black man throughout various stages of his life as he explores his sexuality and who he fundamentally is.
reviews.author: Patricia Karounos

reviews.text: Widely regarded as one of the most intimate and well-made movies of all time, Moonlight is nothing short of a masterpiece, every element coming together to create an experience that can be appreciated by all.
reviews.author: Rebecca Johnson

reviews.text: It is so clear that Jenkins is paying respect to the people he knew growing up and the boy he was. Moonlight is honest and open, exactly what a movie of this type should be.
reviews.author: Tina Kakadelis

reviews.text: Beautifully shot, dynamically acted, and with a magnificent score, it is the type of film that only grows more emotionally potent as time passes.
reviews.author: Chase Hutchinson

reviews.text: Jenkins portrays a world so often fetishized and reduced to its most violent outcomes from the inside, with tenderness and Wong Kar-wai’s influence on his cinematic sleeve.
reviews.author: Andrea Thompson

reviews.text: There are very few coming-of-age films that are more delicate, intimate, and utterly bewitching than Barry Jenkins’ Moonlight.
reviews.author: Mark Johnson

reviews.text: Gorgeous to look at and accompanied by an exquisite soundtrack.
reviews.author: Jennifer Bisset

reviews.text: The film is a stunning portrayal of a young black man at three stages of his life and features sizzling performances by an amazing ensemble cast and lush cinematography by James Laxton.
reviews.author: Brian T. Carney

reviews.text: The director's filmmaking radiates a poetry in his storytelling and visual aesthetic, creating a film that resonates with the viewer in the head and heart.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: Ending as enigmatically as it begins, Moonlight is a film about the lives that slip between the cracks. Its unmissable.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: Moonlight is one of the very best films of the year so far. It is a reminder that despite background, geographic location, race, or sexual orientation, everyone seeks comfort, shelter, someone, and a space in which we can truly be ourselves.
reviews.author: David Gonzalez

reviews.text: The cinematic treatment leaves this diminutive urban story feeling grand, classical and majestic.
reviews.author: Ben Turner

reviews.text: A refreshing, bracing break from not just what Hollywood churns out, but also from the awards-driven independent films that dominate the end of the year.
reviews.author: Kip Mooney

reviews.text: Black lives matter in the quiet, contemplative Moonlight, but let's not stop there.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: A majestic film of gentle moments and pregnant silences.
reviews.author: Olly Richards

reviews.text: What makes Moonlight so amazing is that it almost shouldn't work at all. It is a character study with no lead actor.
reviews.author: Ian Brill

reviews.text: Moonlight displays the kind of empathy and humanity that we desperately need right now.
reviews.author: Nijla Mu'min

reviews.text: A movie that beats with a very human heart while subverting expectations with almost every scene.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Moonlight is one of the best movies of the year from a new and exciting voice in cinema. With his second film, Berry Jenkins shows a maturity beyond his years...
reviews.author: Rudie Obias

reviews.text: A fascinating character study that is sometimes tender, sometimes ferocious, yet always profound.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: [Delivers] as both a remarkable exercise in sensuousness and a wholly affecting look at suffocated identity.
reviews.author: Luke Gorham

reviews.text: A deconstruction of traditional masculinity as a societal prison, [Moonlight] never asks for compassion -- it entrusts its viewers to contain it within themselves.
reviews.author: Matt Cipolla

reviews.text: Right from the beginning, Moonlight makes its impact known. You're watching a reaffirmation of black culture by telling it from a different perspective and understanding.
reviews.author: Kelechi Ehenulo

reviews.text: To not understand the life depicted here is to not have humanity.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: The dialogue is exquisite, but the most powerful moments come from silence... intimate moments to reflect and comprehend Chiron's reality. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ricardo Gallegos

reviews.text: Unique and universal, bleak and hopeful, compassionate and humane, Moonlight eschews ordinary answers, constructs, and definitions.
reviews.author: Brent McKnight

reviews.text: Relying on intensely naturalistic performances and situations, it somehow manages to smuggle in moments of interior lyricism without breaking the flow of the film[.]
reviews.author: CJ Sheu

reviews.text: It's the social commentary on an intimately sincere human reality. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: It's very good.
reviews.author: Andrew Galdi

reviews.text: A less pretentious, more poignant and powerful Boyhood.
reviews.author: Avaryl Halley

reviews.text: The fact that Moonlight as a film even exists is impressive; but that it's as near-perfect a film as you'll see all year is miraculous.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: Jenkins boils a life down to its decisive moments; a life in three parts is an eloquent and acute summation with Nicholas Britell's heart-rending music underlining.
reviews.author: Elissa Suh

reviews.text: Ultimately, Moonlight is cinema that's vital and profound. If there is any way humanly possible to put this film in front of your eyeballs, you owe it to yourself to do so. This movie is why movies exist.
reviews.author: Tim Brennan

reviews.text: MOONLIGHT is not a portrait painted in broad brushstrokes, but a tapestry - any one strand can be admired for its own technique and qualities, but standing back to observe the whole is where the power lies.
reviews.author: Jim Ross

reviews.text: Barry Jenkins' screenplay is beautiful in its simplicity, relying just as much on its stars' exceptional abilities to move the story along during moments of silence.
reviews.author: Joe Passmore

reviews.text: Moonlight has tremendous value both as unflinching dissection of a long-standing problem in the community and for the depiction of a kid with few choices who is unable to rise above the obstacles in his path.
reviews.author: Jorge Ignacio Castillo

reviews.text: The film is largely about the physical and emotional violence that's done to Chiron that enmeshes him in silence, against the grain of the slim moments of inexplicable kindness that break through to nurture him towards trust.
reviews.author: Seph Rodney

reviews.text: Beautiful, hopeful and captivating.
reviews.author: Sarah Knight Adamson

reviews.text: Moonlight managed to beautify an area considered horrifically ugly and scarred. The movie also brilliantly tackled black masculinity, crack addiction and bullying with an honest and fresh approach.
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: Moonlight is an achingly beautiful film of tragedy, love, and yearning.
reviews.author: Chris McCoy

reviews.text: Barry Jenkins's screenplay and direction allows room for the entire cast to embody their roles and interact in very real ways.
reviews.author: Leslie Combemale

reviews.text: Jenkins details a nuanced odyssey of identity thwarted by cultural expectations and communal traditions with an emotional depth.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: Moonlight is one of those films that play out like a huge build up towards an emotionally taut final act. Some will find the climax too understated but that's exactly what makes it feel real and powerful, just like the rest of the story.
reviews.author: Alexander Ryll

reviews.text: Confronting, heartbreaking, joyous, illuminating, personal and powerful.
reviews.author: Kate Rodger

reviews.text: A coming (out) of age story that strikes the perfect balance between its exploration of sexuality and its exploration of identity.
reviews.author: Wesley Lovell

reviews.text: 'Moonlight' is an experience subtle enough to establish itself as a remarkable racial drama. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Loser

reviews.text: The only way to describe Moonlight is as art. It's pure, unadulterated art. It's storytelling at it's best. It's filmmaking at it's best. It's romantic, emotional, and, most importantly, a film that needs to be seen.
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: It will forever live as one of the most profoundly touching and mesmerizing films with a fantastic, diverse cast that demonstrated the power of intersectionality.
reviews.author: Hanna B

reviews.text: Those who care deeply about the art of filmmaking and appreciate masterful storytelling will have their world rocked by this powerful film.
reviews.author: Victor Stiff

reviews.text: The film doesn't possess one of those purposefully frustrating indie movie endings where the credits roll the moment the filmmakers ran out of ideas. Moonlight finishes not on a period or an exclamation point, but an ellipsis.
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: Moonlight is everything you've heard; it is a gorgeous, lyrical, spiritual, moving symphony of visual poetry that uses silence as a paintbrush to color the most vibrant muted emotional complexities.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: A deeply human exploration of masculine identity, and how it intersects with race and sexuality.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: A tremendous film.
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: Moonlight is a strange mixture of the old and the new, offering plenty that we've seen before while pushing boundaries that too often remain rigid in mainstream films.
reviews.author: Tom Bond

reviews.text: Moonlight is a visually stunning film made with restrained finesse and hidden themes you'll find only if you look hard enough. If you don't catch it, you'll regret missing out on one of the best films of the year.
reviews.author: Deborah Cornelious

reviews.text: What writer/director [Barry] Jenkins has done here is capture a small experience and endow it with a universality while still maintaining its unique perspective. It is an astonishing feat.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: The actors and this story are at the heart of the film.
reviews.author: Amanda Greever

reviews.text: In times of Ferguson, in the times that Eric Garner lived, it is radical to see Moonlight's Chiron still have enough love to give to Kevin.
reviews.author: Bedatri D. Choudhury

reviews.text: ...holistically beautiful. Its cinematography, its performances, its narrative, its ideas, its moments-there is an aura of empathy and glory surrounding all of it.
reviews.author: Joel Mayward

reviews.text: [Barry] Jenkin's exceptional coming-of-age drama stays firmly planted in your mind by challenging the stilted ways of the past, causing you to look inward and reflect. It's a moving, unshakable piece of cinema that is not to be missed.
reviews.author: James Clay

reviews.text: All the performances throughout are true and quietly heart-rending.
reviews.author: Alexa Dalby

reviews.text: ...a power-driven drama. Jenkins still fuels his small, yet piercing exposition, with a cemented conviction that fortifies the serene rage and manages to instill a convincing dose of sympathy for the periled players in Miami's hidden haven of a hellhole.
reviews.author: Frank Ochieng

reviews.text: The film finds a watchful, plaintive ambience for documenting the legacy of machismo and problematic identity politics at the heart of young black male culture.
reviews.author: PJ Nabarro

reviews.text: It's hard to forget Chiron once you've seen Moonlight.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: Moonlight is a film rammed with fantastic performances. Filled with rich characterisation and powerful moments. it charts three different periods in the life of Chiron, a young, gay black man from inner-city Miami.
reviews.author: Niall Browne

reviews.text: Barry Jenkins' film is a lovely character study that retains its beauty even while examining ugly topics and their ugly effect on society.
reviews.author: Sean Mulvihill

reviews.text: It is an earnest, sensitive rendering of the gulf between being black and being queer, remarkable as a testament to the fact that stories like this are rarely -- if ever -- made.
reviews.author: Tomas Trussow

reviews.text: A relevantly mesmerizing film that daringly tackles a hard concept and accomplishes to make it relatable for everyone.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: Moonlight is an important and vital piece of black cinema, especially now. It's only through visibility that compassion can be nurtured and fostered, transforming solitude and confusion into hope and understanding.
reviews.author: Erik Anderson

reviews.text: It's is a haunting, touching film that somehow, like its name, feels both hyper realistic and dreamlike.
reviews.author: Glynis Costin

reviews.text: I can tell you "Moonlight" is one of the most intimate and beautiful films I have ever seen, and the subject matter might seem so charged that those of us who have not experienced the issues in the film don't even know how to talk about it.
reviews.author: Asia Frey

reviews.text: "Moonlight" is gorgeously shot and wonderfully acted. Director and writer Barry Jenkins sets a high standard for tackling a delicate situation and it stands out in this masterfully woven narrative.
reviews.author: Mae Abdulbaki

reviews.text: If our divided America is looking in the mirror trying to figure out what the future looks like, Moonlight reflects a complex portrait of compassion and community that still feels humanly possible.
reviews.author: Glenn Heath Jr.

reviews.text: The filmmaker's gaze is clear-eyed yet compassionate, and for a self-described straight ally, strikingly queer.
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: This is a film for many eyes to enjoy on many different levels. You may need to try a bit harder finding this film than your average movie release, but it's well worth the dedication.
reviews.author: Avram Vargas

reviews.text: Moonlight demands to be seen on the big screen: It has a physicality and a weight, and its view of Miami is dreamlike and trippy without overplaying the neon and pastel colors that tend to dominate films and TV shows set in that city.
reviews.author: Steve Erickson

reviews.text: Moonlight is awash with both beauty and dignity. I know many of these people, and I suspect most African-Americans do as well.
reviews.author: Lapacazo Magrira Sandoval

reviews.text: The film's originality isn't just in what Jenkins turns the volume way down on. It's what he makes room for.
reviews.author: Darryl Pinckney

reviews.text: It's impressionistic and image-rich, with swirling camera and lush color... a story about men's need to be tender.
reviews.author: Eve Tushnet

reviews.text: A film about a shy person set in a milieu usually defined by ego and confrontation, Moonlight exposes violent male competition as sublimated, psychologically wounding, and pointless but survivable.
reviews.author: A.S. Hamrah

reviews.text: [Barry] Jenkins gets superb performances that are all the more impressive given the relative paucity of dialogue, let alone frank verbal expression of emotions in a deliberately close-mouthed script.
reviews.author: Dennis Harvey

reviews.text: When it comes to the black experience, Moonlight tackles subjects like hypermasculinity and addiction in the aftermath of the War on Drugs.
reviews.author: Michael Arceneaux

reviews.text: Jenkins' authorial voice is resounding and strong and his determination admirable.
reviews.author: Elena Lazic

reviews.text: Part of what makes Moonlight such a revelation is Jenkins' delicate treatment of the inner lives of black men. There's a tenderness we rarely see as the film shines a light on a subculture where too often vulnerability is seen as weakness.
reviews.author: Eli Glasner

reviews.text: Chirón's three sequences of physical confrontation with his surroundings have meaning and motive. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: Moonlight transmits a message of self-acceptance with which any person - regardless of their gender, physical or social condition - can identify themselves... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Arturo Magaña

reviews.text: Moonlight is a beautifully layered film filled with so much emotional content and lyricism.
reviews.author: Al Hoff

reviews.text: Moonlight is a rich and profound character study grappling with questions of race, masculinity, sexuality, class, and love with unerring confidence and poetry.
reviews.author: Ben Nicholson

reviews.text: Stories like Moonlight, told humanely and intelligently, with complexity, nuance, and hope, may help more of its children envision their own.
reviews.author: Larry Mizell Jr.

reviews.text: ...a garden of details. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Antonio Trashorras

reviews.text: ... a detailed description of how helplessness leads to the construction of shells to survive. And how this armor can serve the outside world and the inner, blocking the desire and the ability to communicate, maybe forever. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Gaspar Zimerman

reviews.text: "Moonlight" arrives as a gift, one worth keeping - and regifting.
reviews.author: Lisa Kennedy

reviews.text: Reveals a different type of coming-of-age story that takes a compelling approach to cultural and sexual identity.
reviews.author: Kiko Martinez

reviews.text: Jenkins handles this intimate tale with assurance and delicacy, seducing us with the film's gorgeous photography and drawing us ever deeper into its hero's fraught journey.
reviews.author: Jason Best

reviews.text: Moonlight is a powerful film, exquisitely made, that tells a story of how love can heal all wounds, especially if that love comes from an unexpected place.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: Moonlight is a drama that can be separated from representational politics, but shouldn't be.
reviews.author: Duncan Gray

reviews.text: Moonlight is a fragile and unusual humanistic portrait full of pain and hope, a plea for the acceptance of oneself. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jordi Campeny

reviews.text: Moonlight is one of those rare movies that just doesn't take a wrong step. It is an astounding piece of cinema that compassionately taps into a facet of American life that is not often explored.
reviews.author: Toby Woollaston

reviews.text: Jenkins accomplishes what few filmmakers ever succeed at: to move out of the private story into a historical, social and cultural statement, without one element dominating or even detracting from the other.
reviews.author: Uri Klein

reviews.text: It's a groundbreaking piece of cinematic film...
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: As a melancholy character piece about an inarticulate young man who can't quite become himself no matter how many permutations of his image he puts out into the world, this is strong stuff.
reviews.author: Angelo Muredda

reviews.text: Powerful performances anchor a trilogy featuring a bullied African-American at three stages of his life.
reviews.author: Harvey S. Karten

reviews.text: What is remarkable about Moonlight is that Jenkins and playwright Tarell Alvin McCraney have crafted a film which has this place so deep in its bones that it strikes me as impossible to separate any aspect of its form from the context which produced it.
reviews.author: Phil Coldiron

reviews.text: Stick with Moonlight for some perspective. You'll absorb something good and emerge more reflective about things you've never thought of before.
reviews.author: Nihit Bhave

reviews.text: Moonlight is not just sublime cinema, this is pure art.
reviews.author: Rachit Gupta

reviews.text: The beauty in Moonlight is how it manages to preserve black manhood by actively destroying performative masculinity at every turn.
reviews.author: Ira Madison III

reviews.text: Moonlight is a complicated film, though the elements are so gracefully interwoven it never feels burdensome to the viewer.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: Just go see it. You'll be glad you did. As I said to the publicist after the screening when he asked me for my reaction, It's a movie that will stay with me for a long time.
reviews.author: M. Faust

reviews.text: This is a quiet and powerful film that everyone should try to catch.
reviews.author: Joanne Soh

reviews.text: Moonlight is a film that moves you.
reviews.author: Keeva Stratton

reviews.text: In Moonlight, Barry Jenkins charts an intimate portrait of the plight of young African-American men and nods to the influence of spirituals in the African-American tradition of the Blues.
reviews.author: tt stern-enzi

reviews.text: It is tempting to call it a universal story, a timeless story, but this is too comforting, too glib.It is a specific story, of being queer, black and poor in America - still a story that is little told onscreen.
reviews.author: Anwen Crawford

reviews.text: [Moonlight is] a slice of cinematic poetry with a vision all its own.
reviews.author: Lisa Jensen

reviews.text: Moonlight's beauty is that it shows how the parts of us hidden deep in darkness can still shine brightly.
reviews.author: Ann Lee

reviews.text: Throughout its deeply moving character study, with an all-black cast, "Moonlight" maintains a dynamic energy...
reviews.author: Diane Carson

reviews.text: The masterful level of craft in the film is obvious.
reviews.author: Dorothy Woodend

reviews.text: Moonlight may be a quiet, understated gem. But you can expect the buzz surrounding it to become deafening.
reviews.author: Rick Mele

reviews.text: The five stories' most striking commonality is placing its characters in conflict with the American ideal of being able to forge one's own destiny.
reviews.author: Carla Meyer

reviews.text: Jenkins' handling of Chiron's sexuality is as quietly oblique as everything else in the film.
reviews.author: Rob Gonsalves

reviews.text: Writer-director Barry Jenkins puts the audience inside Chiron's almost constant state of discomfort through the use of silence and close-ups.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: It's a classic, Man.
reviews.author: Blake Howard

reviews.text: Moonlight is a pretty good film that has been embarrassingly over-hyped.
reviews.author: Giovanni Fazio

reviews.text: In Moonlight, moments of physical collision are filmed to emphasise their tactility.
reviews.author: Sarinah Masukor

reviews.text: A delicate and sensitive masterpiece. [Full review in Portuguese.]
reviews.author: Pablo Villaça

reviews.text: Chiron's entire life is filled with so much pain and hardship that you can't help but feel an increasing sense of fear and tension that suddenly, things could go completely and tragically wrong. Imagine living with that fear every day of your life.
reviews.author: Rain Jokinen

reviews.text: Moonlight is a reminder that cinema can be a profound human experience, a means of understanding experiences one may never face.
reviews.author: Stephen Porzio

reviews.text: Through each of their performances, and the rich narrative, Jenkins delivers an authentic, necessary statement of black male self-love.
reviews.author: Candice Frederick

reviews.text: Moonlight is revelation.
reviews.author: Diane Pershing

reviews.text: In this hateful political climate our nation is experiencing, we need more personal stories like the one told by filmmaker Barry Jenkins.
reviews.author: Paul Chambers

reviews.text: Jenkins' skill is in silences, and in his refusal to make people say more than they would -- no grand expository speeches here -- and in the heartache he shows in the faces of the splendid actors.
reviews.author: Rich Heldenfels

reviews.text: Here is a movie designed to make white audiences proud of the tears they shed in a darkened theater because those salty drops of water prove just how sensitive they are, except not really.
reviews.author: Cole Smithey

reviews.text: Moonlight's depiction of conflicted masculinity is built on sophisticated contrasts.
reviews.author: Jason Di Rosso

reviews.text: Jenkins, working with cinematographer James Laxton, makes us feel as if we're right there with Chiron, using handheld cameras that flow sporadically, yet delicately, in and out of scenes.
reviews.author: David Roark

reviews.text: Moonlight is hard to classify; even harder to describe, in terms of its considerable achievements.
reviews.author: Paul Byrnes

reviews.text: The most remarkable thing about Moonlight is how three different actors play Kevin/Chiron, and each version adds resonance to the other two.
reviews.author: Alan Zilberman

reviews.text: Filled with extraordinary performances, Moonlight explores the tension between private and public selves for a closeted black individual who feels pressure to conform to traditional but arbitrary standards of masculinity. [Blu-ray]
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: A cinematic symphony of the patterns and rhythms that come with deciding who you're going to be.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: An excellent, powerful and impeccably acted film. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: Cinematic experiences like this don't come around very often, where you bear witness to a vision that feels both completely fresh, and as universal and deeply personal as film-making can get.
reviews.author: Alex Casey

reviews.text: Jenkins, cinematographer James Laxton and composer Nicholas Britell combine majestically to elevate Chiron's epic to celestial plains.
reviews.author: Hilary A White

reviews.text: Moonlight looks ravishing, but loses the plot.
reviews.author: Camilla Long

reviews.text: Director Barry Jenkins has made known publicly his admiration of Wong Kar-wai, and Moonlight is reminiscent of the Hong Kong auteur's work in both cinematography and feel.
reviews.author: Ben Sin

reviews.text: Simple, beautifully made and finely acted ...
reviews.author: Henry Fitzherbert

reviews.text: I doubt that I will see a better film than Moonlight this year.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: A film where what prevails is a feeling of bewilderment as spectators, amidst great performances and photography. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fausto Ponce

reviews.text: [Moonlight] has freshness, imagination and control that are the marks of true accomplishment.
reviews.author: Nandini Ramnath

reviews.text: Words spoken truly and honestly are hard won in Moonlight, but the film is more than capable of expressing itself in silence.
reviews.author: Hugh Armitage

reviews.text: Moonlight represents American independent cinema at its finest.
reviews.author: Rashid Irani

reviews.text: An almost impeccable achievement. Revelatory filmmaking.
reviews.author: Tom Birchenough

reviews.text: Cinema has been in and around this area time and time again, but Moonlight still feels abundantly fresh and endlessly imaginative.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: Moonlight is a relatively intimate piece. This works to its advantages, certainly, in the final quiet set-piece between Chiron and Andre. It also allows Jenkins to tackle big subjects with care and tact.
reviews.author: Michael Bonner

reviews.text: From the start Moonlight announces itself as something different entirely.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: Life had been scraping along before Chiron was born, and it will likely keep trudging towards an overdose once he is gone. Moonlight is the story of a lifetime, a worthy Oscar contender.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: Material that should by rights be harrowing has become, in Jenkins's hands, euphoric.
reviews.author: Ryan Gilbey

reviews.text: This is a deeply compassionate film that not only does astounding work on the being black, being gay front, but is also about anybody who feels they exist outside the world they've been born into.
reviews.author: Deborah Ross

reviews.text: A film of rare empathy and shimmering beauty.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: I defy anyone not to get completely drawn in.
reviews.author: Jamie East

reviews.text: You won't find a more sensitively rendered, evocative, or surprising coming-of-age film than Barry Jenkins's Moonlight.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: An intense, emotional film with tenderness in every frame.
reviews.author: Allan Hunter

reviews.text: Equal parts poignant and heartening, this is a unique and uniquely told story that deserves to be seen.
reviews.author: Sarah McIntyre

reviews.text: Moonlight is at its most eloquent when its subtext is soft-spoken.
reviews.author: Adam Nayman

reviews.text: The combination of artistry and emotional directness in this film is overwhelming.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: A poem of light and colour, of faces and the play of physique, of passions revealed by glance or gesture.
reviews.author: Nigel Andrews

reviews.text: This is a beautifully made, strikingly acted and powerful drama that has something vital to say about black sexual identity in present-day America.
reviews.author: Matthew Turner

reviews.text: A fascinating portrait of male fragility that knows how to use all the problems that plague its protagonist to offer a portrait as delicate as interesting. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: A genre-defying film. Its visual splendour belies its tough, surface-level subject matter, while the performances pull us deep below that surface with their soulful naturalism.
reviews.author: Dan Jolin

reviews.text: Sensitive, subtle and heartfelt, Jenkins' genre-buster is a significant work that will knock you out.
reviews.author: Rob James

reviews.text: A radically disheartening film of beautifully disturbing and forceful images that tries to transmit moods and vital drives by strictly audiovisual means. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Ayala Blanco

reviews.text: The best film among the Oscar's Best Picture nominees, Moonlight glows like an iridescent animal, tender in touch and sensitive to the complexity of life.
reviews.author: Kong Rithdee

reviews.text: Nothing is forced in this beautiful film. The emotions are describe in an exquisite way, there are no moral judgments and doesn't seek resources to move the viewer. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Boyero

reviews.text: The visuals distracts from the drama, taking away harshness to a hostile and inclement landscape. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Hugo Hernández Valdivia

reviews.text: The whole film is resolved in an indefinite, fragile and at the same time indestructible space, in which everything relevant acquires its authentic value. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Martínez

reviews.text: A story capable of subvert class and of race topics in a clever way with a deep and human portrait that annihilates various prejudices and archetypes along the way. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Daniel de Partearroyo

reviews.text: A film that explores solitude, uncertainty and it's intimate and possesses beauty. The filmmaker relies on sounds and camera locations that allow you to feel what the protagonist experiences. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Adrián Ruiz

reviews.text: A story of indefinition. Of a life in constant danger of being shattered, not by the lack of options (although also), but by having to choose between many, and no good. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yago García

reviews.text: An authentic, complex, operatic, boldly expressive meditation on the circularity of time, alongside identity and love in all their forms.
reviews.author: Josh Slater-Williams

reviews.text: While the muffled dialogue and slang may stop you from understanding every word, one thing is sure, there is no mistaking the powerful statement this exploration of the Afro American male makes.... The subject matter is tough; the experience is touching
reviews.author: Louise Keller

reviews.text: This is a remarkably good movie about one man trying to find love and his place in the world.
reviews.author: Matthew Toomey

reviews.text: In Moonlight sex and sexuality are key. However, it's a strangely asexual film. A more like a thesis about desire more than a cinematographic experience. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Daniel Krauze

reviews.text: Moonlight may not be a film for everyone, but it's a film everyone should be encouraged to see.
reviews.author: Theolin Tembo

reviews.text: What it does manage to say -- be it about community, tolerance, gay masculinity or most obviously, the concept of inevitability -- it puts across beautifully and poignantly.
reviews.author: Amy West

reviews.text: A beautiful and noble film (could be seen as a sort of african american version of Boyhood), but far from that less than revolutionary spirit that a lot of american critics and the Hollywood Academy itself exalted. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: An intimate and haunting drama.
reviews.author: J. R. Jones

reviews.text: A film that insists on a reflective narrative advance, with no special effects of great spectacularity, providing an alternative vision of that tragic determinism that dictates the life of the African American ghetto inexorably. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alberto Sáez Villarino

reviews.text: Jenkins gives us a sensitive chronicle of growth, maturation and self-acceptance. A remarkable film. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ernesto Diezmartinez

reviews.text: Although it's not bad, I found it overrated, as it tells a story through a trite narrative formula and flat characters that we've already been seen in dozens of films. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fernanda Solórzano

reviews.text: One of the best films of 2016, that tells us that our humanity emerges when we feel empathy and compassion. When we see each other and learn to forgive ourselves. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mario P. Székely

reviews.text: A well-made, simple and unpretentious film that reflects in a sensitive and profound way around the human condition. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Lucero Solórzano

reviews.text: One of the most important and urgent premieres to watch, as it tackles the topics it talks about with integrity, ambiguity and lots of dignity. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Gonzalo Lira Galván

reviews.text: Smaller and more modest than other great productions this story has subtle yet powerful attributes. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: A film that, rather than responding to tendencies or needs of genres or easy labels, finds its power in the humane through a viscerality of various nuances that finds a unique eloquence in its cast. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge (JJ) Negrete

reviews.text: A personal/political triptych which offers keen perspectives on masculinity, queer sexuality, racial identity, and the odd angles at which they intersect.
reviews.author: Charles Bramesco

reviews.text: It's one of those rare films that actually hits you the hardest the moment it finishes, when, all of a sudden, you realise what it is that you've actually been watching.
reviews.author: CJ Johnson

reviews.text: We've seen movies and television about this sort of man before, and one of Moonlight's strongest assets is the way it refines this character type, subverting the narrative.
reviews.author: Glenn Dunks

reviews.text: There's possibility in every moment, as you see when Chiron reconnects with the grown Kevin (Andre Holland), and those moments keep accumulating until Moonlight is an unforgettable vision of love and acceptance.
reviews.author: Craig Mathieson

reviews.text: The performances are all very good indeed, and the film's serious, concerned tone suits the subject matter.
reviews.author: David Stratton

reviews.text: What begins as an arresting blend of lyrical storytelling and bad-neighbourhood harshness gradually ferments into a relentlessly melancholic dirge in dire need of somewhere to go...an early contender for the most overrated film of the year.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: An essential experience that has the definition of identity as a central theme, which is presented with an elegant and sometimes romantic style. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alonso Díaz de la Vega

reviews.text: This remains a story about dignity and, despite everything, beauty, with fine, naturalistic acting throughout and often gorgeous cinematography capturing the stark sunlight (and rich moonlight) of southern Miami.
reviews.author: David 'Mad Dog' Bradley

reviews.text: So much is left unsaid in Moonlight. But nothing is left unfelt.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: This is unmissable.
reviews.author: Tara Thorne

reviews.text: A film that proves to have an extraordinary sensitivity to address the internal drama of its main character, an outstanding identity and solidity. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ezequiel Obregón

reviews.text: It's going to take something spectacular to come along and knock Moonlight off its perch because it may very well be the best movie you'll see this year.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: The societal import of a work of art - in this case Moonlight - is vital to our understanding of it as a whole but should not make a work of art beyond reproach.
reviews.author: Chris Rudd

reviews.text: In shot after shot the movie puts you vividly in its hero's headspace -- to stunning effect.
reviews.author: Nick Dent

reviews.text: With the precision of a cinematic diamond cutter, filmmaker Barry Jenkins has crafted a great three-chapter chronicle...
reviews.author: Liam Maguren

reviews.text: This may be a movie that is keeping it real for most of its time on screen but in the end, Moonlight fair glows with possibility and hope.
reviews.author: Russell Baillie

reviews.text: There are too many quality aspects, particularly the performances, to ignore this film, which has stimulated much discussion.
reviews.author: Damien Straker

reviews.text: Moonlight defies more than the movies. It defies the way we identify ourselves as well. If you're looking for shorthand, call it the portrait of a person. Say it's also beautiful to behold, and brilliant.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: Jenkins doesn't just show us the experience of his young protagonist, he bathes us in it.
reviews.author: Amber Wilkinson

reviews.text: Coming together with a pace that is deliberate but never sluggish, Moonlight is a beautifully human cinematic experience, and something to behold.
reviews.author: Eric Eisenberg

reviews.text: Moonlight depicts an American story of which America needs to be reminded.
reviews.author: Brad Keefe

reviews.text: Moonlight is a film full of mesmerizing mystery. As it slowly searches through a young man's conflicted heart, it creates a moment-to-moment feeling of discovery. It leaves you with a sense of pure wonder.
reviews.author: Sam Watermeier

reviews.text: There are several movies' worth of themes to consider in this single, deeply felt drama of elegant, heartbreaking simplicity.
reviews.author: Eric D. Snider

reviews.text: Right down the line, every single actor in the large cast paints a remarkable, unhurried, true-to-life portrait.
reviews.author: Kelly Vance

reviews.text: The multiple names place Chiron within the historical context of American racism: It's a reminder that he is a resident of a country that stripped his ancestors of their cultural and literal identities.
reviews.author: John Beifuss

reviews.text: It's a special feature, rich with character and perspective, and it showcases what Jenkins is capable of, especially with difficult tales of lives lived in a constant state of fear.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: A film with a name that radiates delicacy and shines with the simplicity, with a story simple but deep; hard and beautiful at the same time. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pilar Ayuso

reviews.text: Is a portrait of life written with cut-to-the-bone honesty. That's what makes Moonlight so arresting
reviews.author: Leonard Maltin

reviews.text: Whether you see Moonlight as a perfect movie or not, it's difficult to imagine that you won't be moved by the way Jenkins interprets and reimagines Tarell Alvin McCraney's play.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: The last third of Moonlight is certainly the most invigorating .
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: The performances in this film are as powerful as the emotions in the story itself. This is a great story about a man who, despite all the suffering he has been through in life, has somehow maintained his dignity and his humanity.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: Little if any of this covers any real new ground, but there's something about the way Jenkins has assembled & presented it that makes the story, characters, & themes feel fresh. (Full Content Review - Violence, Profanity, etc. - also Available)
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: Although Barry Jenkins' film is indeed about the struggles and difficulties of a person embracing his culturally reviled sexuality, the story is universal in scope and intent.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Besides being one of the year's best films, Moonlight crowns itself as the most important. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: Despite its rough exterior, "Moonlight" is a tender picture, a soft and understanding portrait of isolation, of living in the shadows by denying one's true self.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: Sixteen years in the life of a gay, poor, and bullied black man whose quest for wholeness touches our hearts.
reviews.author: Frederic and Mary Ann Brussat

reviews.text: Though Moonlight employs a stylistic, arthouse approach as opposed to a traditional narrative, it is nonetheless an important one to watch for people of all walks of life.
reviews.author: David Fontana

reviews.text: The film doesn't offer any kind of soothing balm for our troubled times. What it does offer is a powerful affirmation of its characters' complex humanity.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: relies heavily on quite a few familiar clichés, but mostly transcends them by emphasizing their universality, which makes Moonlight more than a black film or an urban film or a gay film
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: There's not a false performance or detail in it.
reviews.author: Philip Martin

reviews.text: There is no justice in the world if Mahershala Ali does not get a best supporting actor nod for Moonlight.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: Despite its melancholy, and at times upsetting subject matter, Moonlight is a film with a genuine, openhearted message: love survives. Surely the hardest of hearts would be moved by this beautiful film.
reviews.author: Kyle Aaronson

reviews.text: Exquisitely conceived and beautifully realized, Moonlight is one of 2016's most radiant and must-see films.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: 'Moonlight' is a rarity in cinema. And like all rarities, it deserves to be held close, lovingly examined, and treasured.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: A masterpiece - one of the most incredible films of this year. Or any year.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: The indie drama touches on themes of race, sexuality and isolation in ways that are rarely depicted in cinema.
reviews.author: Mara Reinstein

reviews.text: An audacious, emboldening injection into the fabric of the American consciousness, a film that will be remembered as a watershed among followers as the reality of modern film is carved into the walls of important history.
reviews.author: David Keyes

reviews.text: A powerful, timely tale of lost youth.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: Jenkins' ensemble might be the year's finest, with Naomie Harris, as the boy's crack-addicted mother, and likely winner Mahershala Ali, as a kindly drug dealer, of all things, surely to earn Best Supporting Actress and Actor noms, respectively.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: It's only Jenkins' second feature, but Moonlight feels more like a hard-earned career-capper rather than the career-igniter that it should become.
reviews.author: Daniel Barnes

reviews.text: Moonlight is one of the most poignant, poetic and beautiful movies of the year.
reviews.author: Sandy Schaefer

reviews.text: If you're looking for a moving story, artfully told by a filmmaker on the rise, Moonlight certainly warrants the hype.
reviews.author: Christopher Lawrence

reviews.text: It's somehow hard to define great direction-it's easier to define its absence-but Jenkins is surely a great director. He's got it all and more.
reviews.author: Richard von Busack

reviews.text: I'm in love with these characters. I can't stop thinking about them. And I can't wait to see this movie again.
reviews.author: Molly Laich

reviews.text: One of the year's most provocative and sensitive films. And one of the best.
reviews.author: Michael Smith

reviews.text: Moonlight takes the concept of the bildungsroman to its natural end point in ways that many coming-of-age stories don't.
reviews.author: Josh Spiegel

reviews.text: Luminous and plaintive, Moonlight is emotional virtual reality, transforming a unique human experience into something universal and unforgettable.
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: ... practically vibrates with authenticity, a sense of unique place and unsure purpose, gliding like a dream from which one doesn't wish to awaken.
reviews.author: Steve Persall

reviews.text: The visuals are lush, the performances are lived-in, and the story is lyrical, if painstakingly subdued.
reviews.author: J. Olson

reviews.text: An anguished, achingly affecting, incandescent, coming-of-age story - shattering stereotypes of the LGBTQ community.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Moonlight is both a disarmingly, at times almost unbearably personal film and an urgent social document, a hard look at American reality and a poem written in light, music and vivid human faces.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: It's the inner more than outer intensity -- the compassion and dignity in Chiron's ongoing identity crisis -- that stays with us at the end of this brilliant, lyrical work.
reviews.author: Barry Paris

reviews.text: ...has many good moments, with some of the best coming in quiet passages when the camera is still and we can focus on the interactions of the characters.
reviews.author: Sarah Boslaugh

reviews.text: It isn't for black audiences or art-house audiences or liberal audiences or whatever reductive cultural niche people might try to shove it into. Simply, it is one of the most striking films of the year and it is, I believe, for everyone.
reviews.author: Josef Braun

reviews.text: A life, any life, is a collection of moments - and the beauty of writer-director Barry Jenkins' incandescent drama Moonlight is how he crystallizes three moments in the life of a young African-American man into a film that's so moving and beautiful.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: It's one of the best things you'll see all year.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: "Moonlight" is a poetic and poignant story of immense and oppressive loneliness.
reviews.author: David Frese

reviews.text: This is a remarkable film in every way.
reviews.author: Jeff Simon

reviews.text: Basking in this "Moonlight" is one of the cinematic joys of the year.
reviews.author: Calvin Wilson

reviews.text: At times, Chiron's life is heartbreaking, but the film ends with a life-affirming, yet understated, message. Moonlight deserves a spot among the most provocative films of the year.
reviews.author: Julie Washington

reviews.text: A soulful, meditative character study of a character who doesn't even understand himself.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: Jenkins's setups and scenes are remarkably perceptive, and quietly textured.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: [Moonlight's] uncanny blend of strong visuals, social issues, sexuality themes and urban life is a potent mix.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: Jenkins ... tends to try on different modes, as though looking for ways to drape style around the story's bones.
reviews.author: Robert Horton

reviews.text: A work of extraordinary empathy about the kind of character we seldom meet at the cinema.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: An intimate tale that will leave you deeply affected [and] one of the best films of 2016.
reviews.author: Jacqueline Coley

reviews.text: A searing coming-of-age tale, one that goes well beyond any genre boundaries to resonate in a universal way.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: It's a coming-of-age tale writ large, yet director Barry Jenkins renders it so small and intimate you almost feel like you're eavesdropping.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: A unique, brilliantly acted twist on an indie coming-of-age film.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: This isn't simply Jenkins' sophomore effort -- it's the defining pivot of his career, and one of 2016's most essential pictures.
reviews.author: Andy Crump

reviews.text: [Moonlight recalls] works from filmmakers as varied as Richard Linklater, François Truffaut, Fernando Meirelles, Cheryl Dunye and Spike Lee. But, in the end, the director makes this motion picture its own uniquely satisfying enterprise.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: Jenkins lets the scenes play out with organic ease, and cinematographer James Laxton physicalizes the locations with a kind of off-kilter poetry.
reviews.author: Ken Eisner

reviews.text: Moonlight's best moments come in Little's reaction to Juan's affection, but later scenes of Chiron's erotic confusion and Black's maudlin self-pity (he wears muscular drag yet succumbs to weakness) insist that viewers feel sorry for black gay males.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: Jenkins accomplishes a feat of narrative genius. The three stories of Little, Chiron, and Black, could exist separately as shorts... Still, we see them as one character in different stages.
reviews.author: Rubin Safaya

reviews.text: The film left me tremendously sad at the near hopelessness of these lives, but also invigorated by the power of Jenkins' storytelling, at once achingly specific and utterly universal.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: "Moonlight" is a film of rare grace - a tender, compassionate, restrained look at a life lived in the shadows.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: All it takes is a moment to change your life. One encounter, a tiny handful of friendships, a few life turns, fewer than you might imagine, this way or that. Barry Jenkins' exquisite character study Moonlight understands this.
reviews.author: Joe Gross

reviews.text: Barry Jenkins' Moonlight is a deeply personal, deeply expressive film, unlike anything I've ever seen before.
reviews.author: Max Weiss

reviews.text: Chiron's life experiences have almost all been bad but, in the end, the character is given a glimmer of hope and possible happiness.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: Truly, madly, deeply: There's magic in this Moonlight.
reviews.author: Steve Davis

reviews.text: Bullying, poverty, closeted sexuality, drug abuse, and racial strife combine to form an overworked agenda of cultural woes that's more concerned with rubber-stamping issues than telling an original story.
reviews.author: Scott Marks

reviews.text: In its quietly radical grace, it's a cultural watershed - a work that dismantles all the ways our media view young black men and puts in their place a series of intimate truths.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: A deeply personal and visually mesmerizing drama that just might be the year's best movie.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: As good as [Hibbert, Sanders and Rhodes] all are, it is Holland who makes the strongest impression, the director's alter ego in guiding this young man towards the light.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: It's less a story than a collection of moments, which leaves its viewer feeling moved and changed, as if you've spent time in someone else's dreams and woke up understanding who they are.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: It may cast a spell on anyone who has known loneliness, exclusion, feelings of inferiority or a desire to be encased in a hard shell to protect a soft interior.
reviews.author: Lawrence Toppman

reviews.text: If you're patient enough to stick with it, the emotional payoffs are profound.
reviews.author: Cameron Meier

reviews.text: Moonlight is a story that needed to be told and is achingly beautiful every step of the way.
reviews.author: Yasmin Kleinbart

reviews.text: Every piece of Moonlight is staged in service to a humanist question: What would love mean to a boy who's been conditioned to hide?
reviews.author: Chance Solem-Pfeifer

reviews.text: The film soon moves from the familiar to the foreign, becoming a textured exploration of black masculinity and coming-of-age that plumbs beyond clichés and stereotypes.
reviews.author: Cary Darling

reviews.text: A decidedly-dystopic, African-American answer to the relatively-sedate, suburban bildungsroman served up by Boyhood!
reviews.author: Kam Williams

reviews.text: "Moonlight" is a minor miracle, a movie that mines beauty out of the ugliest situations, and a glimmer of hope from heartbreak.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: If you think art should challenge us, then you will embrace writer-director Barry Jenkins' exquisitely crafted drama Moonlight. It's a true American masterpiece and one of the best films of the decade.
reviews.author: Tirdad Derakhshani

reviews.text: Aided by beautiful, stereotype-shattering performances and subtle but rich cinematography, it is something heartfelt, stirring and unforgettable.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: ...lit with what can only be described as the aching color of compassion.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: This is a humane movie, one that's looking to prompt empathy and introspection most of all. On those terms, Moonlight is one of the year's most gripping viewing experiences.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: Honest and realistic exploration of one man's journey from a neglectful childhood to adulthood and finding his own - highly personal - way in the world. The main character happens to be black and gay.
reviews.author: Victoria Alexander

reviews.text: This is a vivid and tremblingly lived-in portrait of young black manhood and sexuality, rendered with genuine power and grace. I've never seen anything quite like it, and most moviegoers probably haven't either.
reviews.author: Jason Bailey

reviews.text: Barry Jenkins' second feature is basically Boyhood if it had been made about, well, someone else. That doesn't even begin to unpack the layers and resonances in this startling drama
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: So few unexploitative movies are made about young black men, especially young black gay men, that the overpraise for this frail, sweet, discursive fantasia is understandable -- and forgivable.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: It just needs to be watched and embraced, as an entirely fresh example of the power that great movies can exert on our lives.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: Directing, screenwriting, acting, cinematography and music combine superbly in the movie, which is based on a play by Tarell Alvin McCraney and has been compared to Richard Linklater's Boyhood and Charles Burnett's Killer of Sheep.
reviews.author: Anita Katz

reviews.text: Perhaps other great films will be released between now and the end of the year, but I honestly can't imagine any being as worthy as Moonlight for every top prize.
reviews.author: Randy Shulman

reviews.text: What's most wondrous about Moonlight is that it's an uncommonly small story that has so much going on. Beautiful filmmaking on every level (Splice Today)
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: ...an intriguing yet erratically-paced character study.
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: Barry Jenkins's excellent Moonlight is a film filled with bittersweet ironies.
reviews.author: Kate Taylor

reviews.text: We are continually challenged, yet held close to the heart of the story by its romantic lyricism and, most of all, the spacious humanity of its love for its characters.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: In this film, with minimal plot and dialogue, [Jenkins] brings his camera up close to his characters. Without telling us how to feel, he gives us the space to feel Chiron's inner thoughts.
reviews.author: Carrie Rickey

reviews.text: Jenkins crafts cinematic poetry that will echo through to his next movie and beyond
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: "Moonlight" is gorgeous and yet bleak, uplifting and yet sobering, exhilarating but also grounded in some unshakable realities.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Moonlight is incredible -- poetic, haunting, gorgeous, ambitious.
reviews.author: Lauren Chval

reviews.text: This is a wholly special and candidly heartfelt film.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: It's so good it may restore your faith in cinema.
reviews.author: Liz Braun

reviews.text: A perfect film, one that exemplifies not only the formal and aesthetic capabilities of a medium at its most visually rich, but a capacity for empathy and compassion ...
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: Barry Jenkins' character study Moonlight proves to be every bit as luminous, mysterious and elemental as its title.
reviews.author: Dann Gire

reviews.text: "Moonlight" is Miami's first bonafide movie masterpiece.
reviews.author: Rene Rodriguez

reviews.text: "Moonlight" exerts a tidal pull on your heartstrings, but honestly: It's better than that.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: Every year, we get only a few of these, movies that come out of nowhere, that are different, unexpected and wonderfully right. "Moonlight" is that kind of movie, one of the gems of 2016.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: A moviing coming of age story of self discovery that should resonate with audiences and at Oscar time.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: Consider the thin and thick wallops of blue... Blue, blue, electric blue. Lazy blue. Electrified blue. Wash of water. Ice-blue buzz of fluorescence. Azul, azure, lapis lazuli, teal, turquoise, sea, seafoam, sky, cerulean, cobalt...
reviews.author: Ray Pride

reviews.text: Moonlight, then, is subtle and evocative, as much a sensory experience as a linear journey.
reviews.author: Julia Felsenthal

reviews.text: It's possible to appreciate "Moonlight" purely on an intellectual level. But if you happen to be gay - and especially a gay person of color - you will know exactly what a truly monumental achievement this film is.
reviews.author: Martin Tsai

reviews.text: Mostly, [Jenkins] keeps you immersed in one young man's moment-by-moment sensations and emotions. That's a lot.
reviews.author: Stuart Klawans

reviews.text: Jenkins burrows deep into his characters' pain-seared memories, creating ferociously restrained performances and confrontational yet tender images that seem wrenched from his very core.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: It's a coming-of-age story that admits no one ever truly comes of age. We make choices and change shapes.
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: Hopefully it doesn't take Jenkins another eight years to make a film. But we can take comfort in the very strong likelihood that, even if it does, it will be well worth the wait.
reviews.author: Lindsey Bahr

reviews.text: This is a movie set in an on-screen world that feels familiar, the American inner city, in this case one of Miami's toughest neighborhoods. But it meticulously defies the conventions typically associated with movies about that milieu.
reviews.author: Robert Levin

reviews.text: Cinematic poetry and one of the best films of the year.
reviews.author: Annlee Ellingson

reviews.text: He takes a while getting there sometimes, but director Barry Jenkins combines the personal and the political better than almost anyone.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: It's a compelling and resonant drama that gets way under the skin and stays there.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: This is a quiet, modestly scaled film -- a character study made by a filmmaker blessed with unusual amounts of curiosity about his characters that demands an equal commitment of patience from its audience -- but the payoff is beautiful.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: Heartbreaking, mature, unforgettable coming-of-age drama.
reviews.author: S. Jhoanna Robledo

reviews.text: Director Barry Jenkins has somehow figured out how to envelop this turbulent story in an atmosphere that's achingly tender and even beautiful.
reviews.author: Tom Gliatto

reviews.text: It's a touching film that sensitively explores one person's search to find out who he is.
reviews.author: Neil Rosen

reviews.text: Deeply affecting, Moonlight is a small, beautifully told story that resonates well beyond the time spent in the theater.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: Jenkins' emotionally resonant and ambitious approach to filmmaking allows the picture to outshine its shortcomings.
reviews.author: Daniel Gelb

reviews.text: Well-acted with exquisite cinematography and has its fair share of poignant moments, but it falls short of reaching the heights of powerful coming-of-age classics like Boyhood.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: Exhilaration and melancholy are dispensed in equal doses by Moonlight, destined to be one of the better-reviewed films of this year, and for good reason: It's a masterpiece -- an overused word, but not the wrong one.
reviews.author: John Anderson

reviews.text: By the end, you may long for a fourth chapter.
reviews.author: Ella Taylor

reviews.text: There is so much pain in "Moonlight" that it's a little hard to breathe at certain moments. But there are others, of connection and redemption, that positively glow.
reviews.author: Sara Stewart

reviews.text: Moonlight provides a candid, achingly melancholic portrait of marginalization in America.
reviews.author: John Semley

reviews.text: An important and affecting piece of LGBT cinema that comes at a time when the world (and especially this nation) needs more stories like it.
reviews.author: Jason Zingale

reviews.text: A haunting piece of high art.
reviews.author: Leah Pickett

reviews.text: Moonlight tells a coming-of-age story in passages, each possessed of enough stand-alone power to operate as a wonderful short film, even as the whole proves much greater than the sum of the parts.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: Jenkins mounts no soapboxes and brandishes no manifestos in his attempt to illuminate the inner life of this troubled boy turned teenager turned man. Instead he shows us the love that other characters feel for Chiron ...
reviews.author: Dana Stevens

reviews.text: Easily one of the most personal and most powerful films of the year.
reviews.author: Chris Nashawaty

reviews.text: Barry Jenkins' game-changer about growing up black, gay and alienated in the Miami projects is both intimate and epic. It gets inside your head, makes you see the world with new eyes- and then it owns you.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Moonlight is a film so measured, so delicate and powerful, that it proves to be sensitive in ways most movies aren't, even in ways most of life isn't.
reviews.author: Will Leitch

reviews.text: "Moonlight" is magic.
reviews.author: Kenneth Turan

reviews.text: A question is posed to the main character of Barry Jenkins's wondrous, superbly acted new film, Moonlight: "Who is you, man?"
reviews.author: Melissa Anderson

reviews.text: Hype would bruise Barry Jenkins's Moonlight, which is so delicate in its touch that the usual superlatives sound unusually shrill. It's the gentlest, most suggestive of great films.
reviews.author: David Edelstein

reviews.text: A work of art all its own, thoughtfully made and deeply affecting.
reviews.author: Stephen Danay

reviews.text: Floridly shot, richly humanistic drama about a young man coming of age in a rough Miami slum tangles with love, violence, identity, addiction and sexuality.
reviews.author: Chris Barsanti

reviews.text: By the end, calling "Moonlight" an "important" film seems like an insult. It's even better than that.
reviews.author: Matt Prigge

reviews.text: This achingly beautiful coming of ager leaves its mark on both heart and soul.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: A remarkable drama about a young black American man wrestling with his sexuality in a society already prejudiced against him because of the colour of his skin.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: An elegiac, raw, painful film that explores the strangeness of growing up gay in Miami's black community in the 1980s.
reviews.author: Kate Muir

reviews.text: A nuclear-fission-strength heartbreaker. It's made up of moments so slight and incidental they're sub-molecular - but they release enough heat and light to swallow whole cities at a stroke.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: Moonlight surprised me. Then it rattled me to my core. And finally, it nestled snuggly inside my heart.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: An astonishing film from Barry Jenkins. One of the best films of recent years.
reviews.author: Jon Lyus

reviews.text: Under Jenkins' direction, Moonlight is both haunting and poetic, a bittersweet elegy for what could have been. His unflinching camera, which tends to follow the film's characters like a ghost, gives the film a startling immediacy and emotional power.
reviews.author: Nico Lang

reviews.text: Jenkins has an extraordinary eye for ordinary spaces, the contexts within which his characters must define themselves.
reviews.author: Michelle Orange

reviews.text: A drama that's as frustrating as it is innovative in its storytelling decisions.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: Moonlight feels almost as prescient as it is heartbreaking -- which is to say, profoundly.
reviews.author: Patrik Sandberg

reviews.text: Moonlight moves for a while in heady bursts, like memories rushing back.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: What tends to right Moonlight, even when Barry Jenkins's filmmaking drifts into indulgence, is the strength of its actors.
reviews.author: Sam C. Mac

reviews.text: An emotional but discrete drama about the acknowledgement of homosexuality in an African american young man. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Leonardo Garcia Tsao

reviews.text: Acting as urban cinema's "Brokeback Mountain" and "Boyhood," it's as if we got to see "Ennis" and "Mason" grow up in a different culture and era. In this case, it's even more powerful and profound.
reviews.author: Clayton Davis

reviews.text: Moonlight is proof that stories which are more specific and focused on idiosyncrasies and particulars of individuals are often more equipped to effectively engender universal responses.
reviews.author: Darren Ruecker

reviews.text: It is thrilling, sensuous stuff.
reviews.author: Simran Hans

reviews.text: Humane and deeply moving.
reviews.author: Kenji Fujishima

reviews.text: With repressed men of all races increasingly finding reason to lash out, Moonlight asks us to put down our arms and open our hearts.
reviews.author: Noah Gittell

reviews.text: The work of a major film-maker and not just a promising one.
reviews.author: Sam Adams

reviews.text: A staggering work.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: The acting elevates the clichés of Barry Jenkins's script into something approaching lived truth.
reviews.author: Jake Cole

reviews.text: That rare film that seems to wholly capture a human experience, in all of its tragedy and wonder.
reviews.author: William Bibbiani

reviews.text: Understated and thought-provoking.
reviews.author: Stephen Mayne

reviews.text: Moonlight is mesmerically, sometimes swooningly, shot and scored, and well-acted all round too.
reviews.author: David Sexton

reviews.text: A memorable drama that analyzes the way we relate with each other under modern society standards. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Oscar Uriel

reviews.text: One of Moonlight's remarkable strengths is how completely it avoids preaching, after-school messaging, or pat cinematic answers.
reviews.author: Tasha Robinson

reviews.text: One of the year's best films, one of those movies that sneaks up on you and packs a wallop in the end.
reviews.author: Emily St. James

reviews.text: Leaves you feeling both stripped bare and restored, slightly better prepared to step out and face the world of people around you, with all the confounding challenges they present. There's not much more you can ask from a movie.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: Moonlight is a film that is both lyrical and deeply grounded in its character work, a balancing act that's breathtaking to behold.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: Moonlight is a quietly introspective depiction steeped in unparalleled honesty of the ways in which we're saved and damned throughout our lives.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: A masterpiece of poetic filmmaking, Moonlight is one of the most powerful films of the year.
reviews.author: Oliver Whitney

reviews.text: Moonlight takes the pain of growing up and turns it into hardened scars and private caresses. This film is, without a doubt, the reason we go to the movies: to understand, to come closer, to ache -- hopefully with another.
reviews.author: Joshua Rothkopf

reviews.text: Moonlight is a beautiful piece of filmmaking.
reviews.author: Mike Ryan

reviews.text: Jenkins balances raw honesty with dreamy imagery and keeps his narrative loose, riding emotional beats instead of getting trapped inside a finite beginning and end. That is exactly how it should be.
reviews.author: Radheyan Simonpillai

reviews.text: A triptych illustrating the tidal ebb and flow of identity, Jenkins's film is awash in dreaminess, while still examining the life of one young man with piercing clarity.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: Moonlight is always in tension with itself. Sometimes it wins and turns into something absolutely, rapturously lovely. Sometimes it loses.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: There's warmth and tension in every frame, mostly from characters trying to find the right words or motions to express themselves.
reviews.author: Brian Formo

reviews.text: An indelible portrait of an imperilled life, "Moonlight" is a devastating depiction of masculinity, race and identity. Ambitious in scope but precise in its execution, this deceptively small-scale character piece reverberates with compassion and insight.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: A rarely seen portrait of what it really means to be a black gay man in America today. It's a stunning achievement.
reviews.author: Benjamin Lee

reviews.text: Glows like its title.
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: Barry Jenkins' vital portrait of a South Florida youth revisits the character at three stages in his life, offering rich insights into the contemporary African-American experience.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: The story's power comes from the gaps between words - and an ongoing battle to find the right ones.
reviews.author: Eric Kohn

reviews.text: Jenkins and McCraney have artfully cobbled together something that is impressionistic and wondrous, like a compendium of half-remembered memories, tinged by sadness.
reviews.author: Sam Fragoso

reviews.text: There have simply not been enough films about the gay experience of African-Americans or other people of color for that matter. Is is not hyperbole to note Barry Jenkins' magnificent new drama "Moonlight" is a historic achievement in this regard.
reviews.author: Gregory Ellwood

synopsis: A look at three defining chapters in the life of Chiron, a young black man growing up in Miami. His epic journey to manhood is guided by the kindness, support and love of the community that helps raise him.
